newsitem.title: UK: Truckers say France owes 800 mln frf compensation.
newsitem.headline: Truckers say France owes 800 mln frf compensation.

text.p: The French government still owes truck operators across Europe at least 800 million francs ($138.5 million) in compensation following last November's truck blockades, Britain's Freight Transport Association (FTA) said.
FTA director general, David Green said the 800 million franc bill was a minimum cost to truck operators and was based on a Europe-wide survey, an FTA statement added.
Green is also president of the International Road Transport Union and will today deliver a letter to the French embassy asking President Jacques Chirac for early action on compensation payments.

He added that many truck operators still had to register claims and the figure had been compiled only on vehicle operating costs and did not include subsequent losses due to failed deliveries or spoiled goods.

The FTA statement said that British government had negotiated a compensation package with the French authorities which should have resulted in in claims being paid by now, but:"there are no signs of any payments in the near future." --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +5017 ($ = 5.776 French Francs)
